claims.claim: We searched 7 bibliographic databases (MEDLINE and PsycINFO via Ovid, Web of Science, CINAHL via EBSCO, Scopus, ACM Digital Library, and IEEE Xplore) up to October 2023.

claims.claim: Following a 2-stage screening by independent reviewers, we selected 68 articles that included 94 user evaluations.
claims.evidence_quote: Following a 2-stage screening by independent reviewers, we selected 68 articles that included 94 user evaluations.

claims.claim: Results Most articles (36/68, 53%) report on recommender systems focused on nutrition, with fewer (16/68, 23%) aiming to promote PA.
claims.evidence_quote: Results Most articles (36/68, 53%) report on recommender systems focused on nutrition, with fewer (16/68, 23%) aiming to promote PA.

claims.claim: Most studies on digital nudges (11/68, 16%) targeted nutrition-related nudges for shopping and meal selection (8/68, 2%).

claims.claim: Articles address PA and sedentary behavior less frequently (3/68, 4%).
claims.evidence_quote: Articles address PA and sedentary behavior less frequently (3/68, 4%).

claims.claim: Three out of 68 (4%) articles report on recommender systems in combination with games, and 2 out of 68 (3%) articles report on recommender systems and digital nudges.

claims.claim: Approaches to item retrieval vary widely, with 31 out of 68 (46%) articles failing to describe their methods.

claims.claim: Sixty-eight evaluations report positive results, while 26 studies report mixed, negative, or no-difference results.

claims.claim: Following deduplication, screening, eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal, 50 studies were retained, of which 30 empirically implemented RL-related adaptive techniques and constituted the mapped evidence set.

claims.claim: Multi-armed and contextual bandits were the most prevalent approaches (43.3%), followed by Q-learning and value-based RL (26.7%), actor–critic and policy-optimization methods (16.7%), feedback-aligned RL (6.7%), and model-based planning or tree-search approaches (6.7%).

claims.claim: Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a mechanism for transforming recommender systems from static preference-prediction tools into adaptive decision-support systems that learn from sequential user and environmental feedback.
claims.evidence_quote: Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a mechanism for transforming recommender systems from static preference-prediction tools into adaptive decision-support systems that learn from sequential user and environmental feedback.

claims.claim: However, evidence on how RL is integrated and evaluated within recommender systems relevant to personalized financial decision support remains fragmented across application domains.

claims.claim: This study systematically maps empirical RL-related approaches according to their RL approach, integration role, decision formulation, and evaluation practices.
claims.evidence_quote: This study systematically maps empirical RL-related approaches according to their RL approach, integration role, decision formulation, and evaluation practices.

claims.claim: Across these approaches, RL-related methods supported direct recommendation and policy selection, recommender or strategy selection, model and representation adaptation, and preference elicitation and planning.
claims.evidence_quote: Across these approaches, RL-related methods supported direct recommendation and policy selection, recommender or strategy selection, model and representation adaptation, and preference elicitation and planning.

claims.claim: Reward formulations ranged from behavioral and recommendation responses to utility, revenue, cost, profit, and feedback-derived objectives.

claims.claim: However, direct financial applications were comparatively limited, and evaluation relied substantially on offline and experimental settings, with limited longitudinal and real-world validation against sustained financial outcomes.

claims.claim: The findings demonstrate that effective RL-enabled financial recommendation requires alignment among the decision context, state and action representation, reward function, feedback mechanism, constraints, and evaluation outcomes.

claims.claim: Cette thèse présente quatre contributions au domaine des systèmes de recommandation: (1) nous proposons une implémentation d'un algorithme de recommandation de factorisation matricielle parallélisable pour assurer un meilleur passage à l'échelle, (2) nous améliorons la précision des recommandations en prenant en compte l'intérêt implicite des utilisateurs dans les attributs des items, (3) nous proposons une représentation compacte des caractéristiques des utilisateurs/items basée sur les filtres de bloom permettant de réduire la quantité de mémoire utile, (4) nous faisons face au démarrage à froid d'un nouvel utilisateur en utilisant des techniques d'apprentissage actif.

claims.claim: It encompasses four ideas: 1) distributional input rating, which enables the explicit representation of noise patterns in user inputs; 2) distributional voting profile, which enables the preservation of not only shift but also spread and peaks in user’s rating habits; 3) distributional similarity, which enables the untangled and separated similarity computation of the likes and the dislikes; and 4) distributional prediction, which enables the communication of the uncertainty, granularity, and ambivalence in the recommendation results.
